mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N more than Y', translate it to X = Y + N (add N to Y).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the phrase 'has N more than' appears, indicating a direct relational increase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has 3 more than B" as A = B or A = B - 3, ignoring the +3.

mathgap.title: Allow negative differences
mathgap.principle: When a statement explicitly refers to a signed difference, such as 'the difference between A and B is N', interpret it as A - B = N, allowing the result to be negative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the phrase 'difference between' is used without qualifiers like 'absolute' or 'more than'.
mathgap.example: Treating "the difference between A and B is -5" as 5 instead of -5.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y; apply both changes to the current counts.
mathgap.example: Adding N to the giver instead of subtracting, or adding N to the receiver twice.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every statement into a linear equation, then solve the system (e.g., by substitution or elimination).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple interdependent statements need to be resolved simultaneously.
mathgap.example: Skipping an equation and leaving a variable undefined, leading to an under‑determined system.

mathgap.title: Combined sum interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'X has N more than Y and Z combined', first sum Y and Z, then add N: X = (Y + Z) + N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a phrase mentions a combined group of persons before adding a difference.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has 3 more than Y and Z combined" as X = Y + 3, ignoring Z.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', multiply the original amount by k: new_X = k * old_X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a multiplicative increase is described.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increases by 3 times" as adding 3 instead of multiplying by 3.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and each recipient receives the split amount (original count divided by number of recipients).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes an equal split of all items.
mathgap.example: Leaving the splitter with the original count after splitting, instead of zero.

mathgap.title: Sequential direct assignments
mathgap.principle: When multiple statements assign a direct count to the same person, treat them as occurring in order; later assignments overwrite earlier ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person receives more than one explicit count assignment.
mathgap.example: Treating two "A has N" statements as simultaneous, causing double counting of A's items.

mathgap.title: Absolute difference for 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: In equations of the form 'the number of X that Y has more than Z equals …', interpret the left side as a non‑negative absolute difference |Y − Z|.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equation uses 'has more than' on the left side.
mathgap.example: Treating "the number of apples that A has more than B equals 4" as A = B + 4, instead of |A - B| = 4.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between X and Y' (without qualifiers like 'absolute'), interpret it as a signed difference X − Y, allowing negative results; in mixed equations, treat the right side as signed while the left side may be absolute.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between' appears, especially in equations equating an absolute difference to such a phrase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the difference between A and B" as |A − B|, leading to ambiguous multiple solutions.

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as an initial count before transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given count is final and then adds transferred amounts, double‑counting the items.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply transfers after establishing the initial counts; treat the given count as the starting amount before any transfers.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model forgets to zero out the splitter or to divide equally among recipients.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a split is described, set the splitter's count to zero and distribute the items equally among the recipients.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds to the giver instead of subtracting, or subtracts from the receiver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as signed difference, leading to negative values
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets the left side as X − Y instead of the intended absolute difference |X − Y|.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret the left side of such equations as an absolute (non‑negative) difference.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference, leading to ambiguous solutions
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes 'difference between' always yields a non‑negative value, ignoring the signed nature of the phrase.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'difference between X and Y' as a signed difference X − Y (allowing negative), unless the context explicitly calls for an absolute difference.
